summary.name: DevHub
summary.one_liner: DevHub is an offline, local-first macOS toolbox that bundles many everyday developer utilities (JSON, Base64, JWT, QR codes, hashes, image tools, and more) into one app.
keywords: small developer tools in one app
use_cases: format and inspect JSON, HTML, URL, Base64 and JWT data offline
generate QR codes, barcodes and WiFi QR codes
extract EXIF metadata or blur privacy details in images
generate hashes, passwords and RSA keys
trigger developer tools from Raycast or shell scripts via URL scheme
check timestamps, date conversions and world time
summary.what_it_does:
DevHub is a macOS app that collects many small developer utilities in one place, covering text and encoding, code and data formatting, images and media, productivity and system tasks, and security and network tools. Examples listed include JSON formatting, JWT parsing, Base64 conversion, regex testing, URL parsing, hash and RSA key generation, QR and barcode generation, EXIF viewing, image watermarking, and API requests. The page says it is built primarily for local use and aims to replace scattered web tools and shell snippets rather than an IDE. Tools can be opened through a URL Scheme (devhub://...) from Raycast, browsers, Terminal, or automation workflows. The page lists a large set of completed tools and states an ongoing goal of 100+ utilities with weekly updates.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">unknown
notable: Offline, local-first design with privacy emphasis
URL Scheme support for Raycast, browsers, and terminal automation
Large collection of small developer tools in one app
Available on the Mac App Store (per listing link)
caveats: Requires macOS 14.0 or later according to the README
Collection is still growing; the page describes the 100+ utility goal as ongoing
Pricing is not stated on the page
